To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the immunohistochemistry of cryostat sections of human tonsils is superior to paraffin sections; (2) the immunohistological response of tissues is affected by processing and fixation; (3) the antigenicity of Ig can be improved in paraffin-embedded tissue by treatment with trypsin.

the PAP technique is more informative than the FITC technique for demonstrating Ig in cryostat and in trypsinized paraffin sections and that trypsin is more effective than other proteolytic enzyme in unmasking antigen in paraffi sections.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the demonstration of Ig in cryostat and formalin fixed paraffin embedded sections of human tonsils by means of the immunoperoxidise method and the effects of processing and proteolytic treatment on the immunohistological performance of tissues.
the use of proteases to unmask antigen in sections of paraffin embedded tissues.
the demonstration of Ig in cryostat and formaldehyde-fixed paraffin sections using immunofluorescent and immunoperoxide methods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PAP method is more informative, and the FITC method more sensitive than the PAP method.
the FITC technique is the most satisfactory of the two for the detection of Ig in cryostat sections and the PAP technique is the most suitable for paraffin sections.
trypsinised, formaldehyde-sucrose fixed paraffin sections provide the most satisfactory material for immunohistochemical investigations on human tissue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

paraffin sections are as good as cryostat sections in detecting surface Ig and that paraffin and frozen sections are equally good for detecting intracellular Ig if the paraffin sections have been trypsinised.
cryostat sections of unfixed tissue are superior to paraffin sections for the demonstration of Ig.
paraffin sections are more suitable for immunohistochemical investigations than cryostat sections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immunohistochemistry of human tonsil is best performed with paraffin sections and the PAP method.
the immunohistochemistry of paraffin-embedded tissues can be as effective as that of cryostat sections.
the immunohistochemistry of tissues for Ig is not dependent on the method of fixation or on the use of a particular enzyme to 'unmask the antigen.
